messages:
maria: Heads up — during today's quant bring-up I hit a weird streaming early-stop with the new LlamaX-v2 conversion. Happens when the tokenizer emits two different EOS-like tokens back-to-back.

ashwin: hmm, can you paste the converter output + the model's config.json? :eyes:

maria: sure. snippet from the HF->Redwood converter log: 
```
special_tokens_map: {'eos_token': '</s>', 'additional_special_tokens': ['<end>']}
tokenizer.eos_token: '</s>'
tokenizer.additional_special_tokens: ['<end>']
model.config.eos_token_id: 2
```

and the streaming payload we sent to the runtime: 
```
{ input: "Tell me a short poem.", max_tokens: 40, streaming: true }
```

The model generation actually returns a token stream that includes both `</s>` and `<end>` adjacent in some templates, e.g. `...
</s><end>`. Redwood's stream stop logic currently checks for the configured `eos_token` sequence and stops as soon as it sees `</s>`, but depending on tokenizer splitting that can cause partial pieces of the assistant markup to be dropped.

devon: ah, so it's not a single repeated token, it's two distinct special tokens used by the original training data/template? That would definitely confuse the stop detector. :thinking:

maria: exactly. In our chat template the trainer appended `<end>` after `</s>` to delineate end-of-turn. HF converter kept both as special tokens but we only mapped `eos_token` -> `</s>`.

ashwin: Do we have a repro? any logs from the streaming side that show the exact bytes we saw at the client?

maria: yes — runtime stdout (trimmed):
```
[stream] chunk: "...and there you have it.
"
[stream] chunk: "</s>"
[stream] chunk: "<end>"
[stream] detected_eos: true
[stream] stopped_at_chunk_index: 1   # stopped after seeing </s>
[client] saw: "...and there you have it.
"    # missing the trailing markup the app expects
```

olivia: that explains the HTML-ish assistant wrapper we lost in the UI. For some templates losing `<end>` matters because downstream parsing expects that marker.

devon: proposed fix: during conversion normalize the special tokens so that the converter either: (a) collapses adjacent eos-like tokens into a single canonical eos, or (b) moves any non-eos trailing markers into `additional_special_tokens` but not as `eos_token`. Also update streaming stop logic to consider a ordered list of stop candidates rather than only the single `eos_token`.

maria: I tried a quick local hack: converter now sets `model.config.eos_token = '</s><end>'` (concatenated) and runtime checks for that exact byte sequence in streaming. That fixed the cut but feels hacky because other clients assume a single token.

ashwin: yeah we should avoid concatenating tokens in config. Better to: 1) add a converter step that recognizes duplicated/adjacent eos markers and emits a canonical sentinel token (e.g., `<|assistant_end|>`), plus a mapping table so we preserve identity; 2) add a regression test for streaming where tokenizer outputs multi-token EOS.

devon: can we add a small unit test to the hf-convert suite that simulates a tokenizer returning `['hello', '</s>', '<end>']` and assert the converted config maps only one `eos_token_id` and that the runtime stop watcher will consume both tokens gracefully (i.e., stop but still flush the buffer containing `<end>`)?

maria: +1. I'll open a PR with the converter change and a test. Also adding a tiny runtime tweak: if stop is triggered on token N and token N+1 is in `additional_special_tokens` and matches a known trailing marker pattern, treat it as part of the flush rather than discarding it.

ci-bot: deploy-preview created: https://ci.redwood.dev/builds/4721 — maria/hf-eos-normalize (tests: 12, failed: 0) :white_check_mark:

olivia: great, will run a small end-to-end with the frontend parser. If that passes we should add a note in the onboarding docs: "If your model uses stacked eos markers (e.g., `</s>` + `<end>`), prefer defining a single canonical eos or include the trailing marker in `additional_special_tokens` and ensure parser expects it."

maria: thanks all. leaving a follow-up todo in the PR for ops to double-check Dedicated rollback behavior in case the concatenated-eos hack ever reaches prod. :thumbsup:

ashwin: added to infra playbook. :rocket:
